title: Deep Work: Rules for Focused Success in a Distracted World

audiences: Knowledge workers who need uninterrupted time to learn, analyse, design, code, research, or write
Students and independent creators whose attention is repeatedly broken by messaging, browsing, and social media
Managers able to redesign team communication and protect concentration as well as collaboration
Readers seeking concrete routines rather than another list of notification settings

sources.title: Deep Work
sources.author_or_publisher: Grand Central Publishing / Hachette Book Group
sources.supports: Canonical title, author, publication date, publisher, ISBN, page count, formats, four rules, description, and selected professional reception.
sources.limitations: Sales page and promotional copy; praise is selected by the publisher.

sources.title: The Book Facebook Doesn't Want You to Read
sources.supports: Author's argument, purpose, annotated contents, definitions, four-rule structure, and account of his own practice.
sources.limitations: Promotional author summary rather than independent verification.

sources.title: In Defense of Thinking
sources.supports: Ten-year retrospective on why Newport wrote the book, its intended organisational challenge, and its later reach.
sources.limitations: Author's retrospective interpretation and reported sales.

sources.title: Is deep work the most underappreciated skill for career success?
sources.supports: Definitions, practices, relationship to deliberate practice, limits by occupation, career claims, and explicit counterquestions.
sources.limitations: Friendly interview; Newport answers challenges about his own framework.

sources.title: Why is it so hard to do my work? The challenge of attention residue when switching between work tasks
sources.author_or_publisher: Sophie Leroy; Organizational Behavior and Human Decision Processes
sources.supports: Two experiments showing persistent attention to a prior task and impaired performance after switching, especially around unfinished work.
sources.limitations: Specific experiments on task transitions, not proof of every productivity or career claim in the book.

sources.title: Deliberate Practice and Performance in Music, Games, Sports, Education, and Professions: A Meta-Analysis
sources.author_or_publisher: Brooke N. Macnamara, David Z. Hambrick, and Frederick L. Oswald; Psychological Science
sources.supports: Counterevidence that deliberate practice matters but explains limited performance variance, especially in education and professions.
sources.limitations: Deep work is broader than deliberate practice; definitions and meta-analytic methods remain debated.

sources.title: The impact of the open workspace on human collaboration
sources.author_or_publisher: Ethan S. Bernstein and Stephen Turban; Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B
sources.supports: Two workplace field studies finding that transitions to more open offices reduced face-to-face interaction and increased electronic communication.
sources.limitations: Two organisations and interaction measures; does not establish one universally optimal office design.

sources.title: Can Deep Work Really Work for You?
sources.supports: Management-oriented evaluation of whether workers and organisations can create uninterrupted thinking time.
sources.limitations: Expert discussion and review, not an intervention trial of the complete system.

sources.title: Too busy to focus? Try this
sources.supports: Contemporary assessment that focus is desirable and the substantive difficulty is implementation amid email and social media.
sources.limitations: Short general-audience column rather than a detailed evidence audit.

sources.title: A Review of Cal Newport's Deep Work
sources.supports: Productivity specialist's praise for writing and practices and criticism that deep-versus-shallow framing is too simple for interdependent work.
sources.limitations: One practitioner's conceptual review, not controlled evidence.

sources.title: Deep Work
sources.supports: Large reader aggregate and recurring praise for practical impact alongside criticism of repetition, padding, limited originality, and schedule privilege.
sources.limitations: Self-selected readers, merged editions, mutable counts, and no control for completion or expertise.

workflow.coverage_notes: The author's full annotated structure and extended explanations were checked against publisher metadata, a contemporary author interview, independent cognitive and workplace studies, professional reviews, and a large reader aggregate. No unauthorised full text was used.
next_steps: Optional: compare all detailed examples and notes with an owner-supplied copy before promoting coverage to full-book.
